# The required status check CONTEXT STRINGS for master, as branch protection
# reports them. Read by CB-2100 (comply gate-effect verification) so the rule
# can be evaluated on a runner that has no admin read on the repository.
#
# This file is CROSS-CHECKED, not trusted: whenever the branch-protection API
# is reachable, CB-2100 fails on any disagreement between the two. Do not edit
# it to make a gate look reachable — regenerate it from the API:
#
#   gh api repos/paiml/paiml-mcp-agent-toolkit/branches/master/protection \
#     --jq '.required_status_checks.contexts[]'
#
# Note that these are CONTEXTS, not job names. `ci / gate` is a job inside the
# reusable workflow ci.yml calls; the unrequired top-level job in ci.yml whose
# display name is `gate` reports as plain `gate` and is a different check.
ci / gate
feature-gate
docs build (docs.rs environment)
pmat score
#
# NOT LISTED, DELIBERATELY: `mutation-diff`. It was added to live branch
# protection mid-session by an agent, and reverted. The workflow that produces
# that context (.github/workflows/mutation-diff.yml) exists only on
# feat/cb-2100-gate-effect and is not on master, so requiring the context makes
# EVERY pull request permanently unmergeable -- including the one that would
# land the workflow. A required check whose producer does not exist on the
# default branch is not a gate, it is a deadlock.
#
# Correct order, to be done by hand AFTER that PR merges:
#   gh api -X PATCH repos/paiml/paiml-mcp-agent-toolkit/branches/master/protection/required_status_checks \
#     --input - <<'JSON'
#   {"strict": true, "contexts": ["ci / gate","feature-gate","docs build (docs.rs environment)","pmat score","mutation-diff"]}
#   JSON
# and add `mutation-diff` back to this file in the same change, so the manifest
# and live protection never disagree -- which is the drift CB-2100 exists to catch.
#
# REVIEW REQUIREMENT (CB-1700), set 2026-08-19. master now carries
# `required_pull_request_reviews.required_approving_review_count = 1`; before
# that the block was absent entirely, so the default branch required zero
# approving reviews. Nothing else in the protection config changed — the PUT
# endpoint REPLACES the whole configuration, so the payload was built by reading
# the live state and adding exactly one key; contexts, strict, enforce_admins,
# force-push, deletions, linear-history and conversation-resolution were all
# carried forward verbatim and diffed afterwards to prove it.
#
# REVERSED the same day, deliberately. The consequence above landed exactly as
# written: PR #1021 went BLOCKED / REVIEW_REQUIRED, and GitHub does not let an
# author approve their own pull request. On a repository whose changes are
# produced by agents and gated by CI, a human-approval requirement does not add
# review -- it adds an admin override to every merge, and an override that
# happens every time has stopped being a control.
#
# So `required_pull_request_reviews` is removed again and repo-level auto-merge
# is ON. The gate is now the four required status checks above, which run the
# tests, the lints, the feature matrix and `pmat score` (including a blocking
# `cargo deny check`). That is a real gate: `feature-gate` caught a drifted
# unrun-tests ledger on this very PR, minutes before it would have merged.
#
# CB-1700 FAILS because of this, and that is the honest outcome rather than a
# bug to be silenced. The rule asserts "modern code review needs at least 1
# approving review" and models no posture in which machines produce the changes
# and CI reviews them. Do not edit the rule to make this repository pass; either
# it grows a model of that posture, or this repository stays red on it and the
# reason is written here. Tracked in paiml-mcp-agent-toolkit#1036.
#
# What is NOT weakened, and must not be: `enforce_admins` stays false only
# because the admin override is the break-glass path; force pushes and deletions
# remain disabled; `strict` remains true so a stale branch cannot merge.
